prerequisites: Competencies acquired in previous years' ethics and anthropology courses

learning_outcomes.text: Facilitate critical reflection through ethical principles and dilemmas in the current social context.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Ethics
1. The engineering profession and its moral dimension
2. Basic notions: Freedom, Responsibility, Called to human fullness
3. The purpose of Ethics: The Golden Rule, What is right or good, Personal good and common good, Obligations and suggestions
4. Ethical Analysis of Human Action: The sources of morality, The principle of double effect
Professional responsibility and codes of ethics
Engineering ethics codes: content and limits.
Legal responsibility vs. moral responsibility.
Whistleblowing
Challenger Case (1986)
Safety, risk, and precaution in engineering
Risk analysis: probability, severity, and social perception.
The precautionary principle: origin, scope, and limits.
Safety regulation in engineering
Ford Pinto Case (1970s)
Environmental ethics and sustainability
Environmental ethics: trends and debates.
Carbon footprint, product life cycle, and eco-sustainable design.
Agenda 2030 and Laudato Si': convergences and differences.
Volkswagen Dieselgate Case (2015)
Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
Algorithmic bias, explainability, and transparency.
EU AI Act: risk categories and obligations.
Dilemmas of generative AI: authorship rights, disinformation, deepfakes, responsibility, and damage distribution
COMPAS Case (USA)
Helios Case
Fraud, deception, and integrity in technological innovation
Integrity in R&D: fraud, plagiarism, and data fabrication.
The 'fake it till you make it' culture
Report writing
Conflict of interest, investor pressure, and silencing of engineers.
Responsible Research and Innovation (RRI)
Theranos Case - Elizabeth Holmes (2003-2018)
Business ethics and corporate social responsibility
Stakeholder theory vs. shareholder primacy
Company as a community of people: personalist principle
Corruption, collusion, and unfair competition
Enron Case (2001)
Worker dignity: labor conditions, conciliation, and globalization
The centrality of work in human life: professionalism
Decent working conditions: working hours, rest, fair wage, and mental health
Work-life balance: co-responsibility, teleworking, and organizational cultures
Labor rights in global supply chains and conflict minerals
The engineer as team leader: their duties towards collaborators
Apple/Foxconn Case (2010-present)
Engineering, war, and dual-use technologies
Lethal autonomous weapons: the debate on lethal decision systems.
Offensive and defensive cybersecurity: ethical limits.
Drones, mass surveillance, and privacy.
The engineer and conscientious objection
Palantir Case - War in Ukraine (2022-present)
Ethical leadership, teamwork, and organizational culture
Servant leadership, authentic leadership, and virtue ethics in the professional environment.
Ethics of teamwork
The engineer as an ethical reference in their team
Boeing 737 MAX Case (2018-2019)
Study of the Jubilee Centre Framework for a Virtue-Based Professional Ethics
teaching_methods: In-person classes. Classroom sessions where the professor presents program content, supported by real engineering case analysis and selected readings. Some sessions will project documentary fragments or testimonies from engineers involved in the studied cases.

Case study analysis. Structured discussion sessions around real ethical dilemmas taken from engineering history and current technology. Students prepare the case beforehand and, organized in groups, argue and defend positions before their peers.
Class tests. Brief individual tests conducted at the beginning of some sessions to verify prior preparation of the case or indicated readings.
Group work: case resolution video. In groups of four or five students, a video (12-15 minutes) is made that develops a real engineering ethics case.
Personal reading and autonomous study. Individual reading and preparation of dossier cases before each session, along with personal study of content developed in class.
Tutoring and follow-up. The professor will be available during established office hours to guide students in their study of the subject, case preparation, and group work development.
assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as: 30% Final Exam + 25% Class Tests (average of the 5 best) + 25% Group Video + 10% Attendance + 10% Active Participation. An optional book reading can contribute an additional 10%. For the extraordinary call, students must request inclusion at least five days before the exam period. The final grade for the course will be that of the extraordinary call, even if it is lower than the one previously obtained. The grade obtained in the extraordinary call will be valid, regardless of the ordinary call result; students may fail the course if they do not attend the extraordinary call.
